title: Knowledge Check 4 - Lessons 16-20
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 16-20 - Consulting and Implementation Strategies | Practical Application of Agentforce Sales Expertise. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A stakeholder asks for a new approval step in week nine of a fixed-price build. What is the correct first response?
options: Build it, since goodwill matters more than margin
Refuse, because the scope is locked
Raise a change request with an impact assessment on cost, schedule, and quality
Absorb it into contingency without telling the sponsor
questions.explanation: Every change, whether creep or genuine gain, goes through the same door so the sponsor decides against the triple constraint; absorbing it quietly overspends contingency, and refusing outright removes the client's ability to buy the change.

questions.question: Which single artifact holds risks that have not happened yet, issues that already have, the assumptions your plan rests on, and the dependencies the client owes you?
options: The RAID log
The change order register
The weekly status report
The burn-down chart
questions.explanation: Risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies live together in the RAID log so nothing hides in an email thread, and each entry carries an owner and a date; the other artifacts track a single concern apiece.

questions.question: Two weeks before go-live the testers have forty defects open, twelve of them severity 1. Which action protects both the launch date and the client relationship?
options: Go live anyway and fix everything in hypercare
Run a defect triage with the business to agree which severity 1 and 2 items block go-live, then take a scope or date decision to the steering committee
Push go-live and cut scope immediately without a decision meeting
Extend testing indefinitely and stop reporting status
questions.explanation: Triage converts an emotional defect count into an agreed blocking set, and the steering committee is the tier that owns scope and date trade-offs; going live unilaterally and extending without reporting both remove the sponsor's ability to decide.

questions.question: During a workshop a department head says the new system must work exactly like the old one. What have you actually captured?
options: A confirmed functional requirement you can build to
A non-functional requirement about usability
A solution preference that hides the real requirement, so you keep asking why until you reach the underlying outcome
An acceptance criterion for UAT
questions.explanation: A statement about the old system is a proposed solution, not an outcome, so the correct move is to keep asking why until the business need it protects is exposed; treating it as a functional requirement locks an old workaround into the new build.

questions.question: Which elicitation technique gives you the most reliable view of how work actually happens, as opposed to how people say it happens?
options: Shadowing an end user through a full transaction
A survey emailed to the team
A group workshop
Reading the existing process documentation
questions.explanation: Observing a real transaction exposes workarounds and exceptions that people do not self-report, which is why the more physical and specific the technique, the closer it sits to truth; surveys and documentation both capture the official story.

questions.question: On a stakeholder map, what does an unengaged high-power stakeholder represent?
options: A low priority contact who can be dropped from updates
A risk to the project who needs a targeted engagement plan
An end user who will adopt automatically once the system ships
A sponsor by virtue of their seniority alone
questions.explanation: High power and low interest is the quadrant a project must keep satisfied, so an unengaged high-power stakeholder is a risk requiring a targeted engagement plan; seniority alone does not make someone the sponsor, which is a role the client names.

questions.question: Twelve use cases are all marked Must in the MoSCoW rankings. What does that tell you?
options: The list is complete and safe to sign into the SOW
The Must threshold has become meaningless and you need a forcing constraint to re-rank
MoSCoW was applied correctly and the sponsor can proceed
You should switch the ranking to alphabetical order to settle ties
questions.explanation: When every item is a Must the tier no longer discriminates, so a real constraint such as budget, date, or capacity is what re-ranks the list; signing an undifferentiated Must list into the SOW turns every wish into a contractual obligation.

questions.question: Data quality in the target objects is poor and unverified, and the client wants the highest-value use case shipped first. What do you sequence first?
options: The highest-value use case regardless of the state of the data
Whichever use case the loudest executive sponsors
A data-remediation foundation slice, because a use case is only as good as the data underneath it
Every use case at once to save elapsed time
questions.explanation: Value cannot be realized on unreliable data, so a data-remediation foundation slice comes first even though it is less visible; sequencing the high-value use case onto bad data teaches the organization to distrust the platform.

questions.question: A client wants a thin end-to-end pilot before committing budget to the full build. What is the best artifact to sequence that pilot?
options: A full technical design document covering every object and integration
A change order against the existing statement of work
A steering committee charter defining decision rights
A walking skeleton, one vertical slice through the real stack, that proves the integration and adoption risk
questions.explanation: A walking skeleton runs one true path from user action through automation and integration to output, which exposes integration and adoption risk while it is still cheap; a horizontal layer would prove each layer in isolation and defer the mismatch.

questions.question: A rep converts a Lead whose record type is Enterprise. The rep's profile default Account record type is Standard. What record type does the new Account get?
options: Enterprise, inherited from the Lead
Standard, the new owner's profile default
The org default Account record type regardless of profile
None; accounts created by conversion have no record type
questions.explanation: Conversion assigns the new owner's profile default record type rather than the Lead's type, which is why orgs that need inheritance build an explicit mapping.

questions.question: The Standard and Enterprise teams must use different stage sets on the same Opportunity object. What do you configure?
options: Two Opportunity record types, each assigned a different sales process
Two separate Opportunity Stage picklists
Two page layouts on one record type
A validation rule that hides stages per team
questions.explanation: A sales process defines which global Stage values a record type may use, so two record types each pointed at their own process is the supported pattern.

questions.question: A previously converted Lead shows its Phone field as read-only. Why?
options: The lead was merged into a duplicate
Field-level security was changed during conversion
Converting a lead places the converted lead record in a read-only state that stays linked to the new account, contact, and opportunity
The lead record type removed edit access
questions.explanation: Conversion is permanent and makes the Salesforce-managed lead fields read-only while keeping the link to the created records; it is not a security or record type effect.

questions.question: How many quotes can be the synced quote on a single Opportunity at one time?
options: Only one quote can be the synced quote
Two, one per price book
Unlimited, as long as statuses differ
One per quote currency
questions.explanation: An opportunity can have many quotes but only one synced quote, and syncing another quote demotes the previous one.

questions.question: A rep cannot add a product to a custom price book. What is the most likely cause?
options: The custom price book is missing a currency
The product has no active Standard Price Book entry
The product record type is wrong
The opportunity is already Closed Won
questions.explanation: A product must exist with an active Standard Price Book entry before a custom price book entry can be created, so the missing standard entry blocks the add.

questions.question: A rep edits the line items on the synced quote. What happens to the opportunity?
options: Nothing until the next forecast rollup
The quote automatically unsyncs and detaches
The synced quote pushes the change to the opportunity, updating the opportunity products and amount
The opportunity stays frozen once it is Closed Won
questions.explanation: The synced quote is the source of truth, so editing its line items updates the opportunity products and amount on sync rather than waiting on a rollup.
